items.headline: President Tharman makes first state visit to Malaysia, urges non-transactional ties
items.summary: On his July 12-15 state visit, President Tharman Shanmugaratnam said Singapore-Malaysia relations must never be a purely transactional relationship. Malaysian PM Anwar Ibrahim paid a courtesy call and said the Johor-Singapore SEZ master plan will be finalised soon.

items.headline: Sheng Siong breaks ground on S$520 million Sungei Kadut headquarters and warehouse
items.summary: Sheng Siong broke ground on July 13 on a seven-storey, 61,000 sq m automated distribution centre, its largest-ever investment at about S$520 million, able to support more than 120 stores by 2029. DPM Gan Kim Yong officiated.

items.headline: Lorry driver jailed 13 months for S$1.4 million damage to CTE tunnel ceiling
items.summary: Lai Daohong, 56, was jailed 13 months and fined S$1,000 on July 13 after his over-height lorry, its crane left unretracted, struck the CTE tunnel ceiling at Cairnhill in November 2024, causing over S$1.4 million in damage and a 10-hour closure.

items.headline: Singapore proposes a new 'purposeful endangerment' driving offence carrying up to 15 years' jail
items.summary: The Road Traffic (Miscellaneous Amendments) Bill introduces an offence of purposeful endangerment using a vehicle causing death or grievous hurt, punishable by up to 15 years' jail, caning, lifetime driving bans and vehicle forfeiture. It also lowers drink-driving thresholds.

items.headline: Aperia Group chief charged with laundering S$38 million in a Nvidia-chip fraud case
items.summary: Aperia Group CEO Alan Wei Zhaolun, 50, pleaded not guilty to 11 charges, accused of laundering about S$38 million into a S$55 million Chee Hoon Avenue bungalow, over an alleged conspiracy involving servers with Nvidia chips said to breach US export controls.

items.headline: Sonam Wangchuk's exam-leak hunger strike enters day 17 as opposition urges him to stop
items.summary: Activist Sonam Wangchuk, fasting at Delhi's Jantar Mantar since June 28 over the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak and demanding Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resign, had lost about 8.5 kg by July 14 as his health worsened. Opposition figures including Akhilesh Yadav appealed to him to end the fast.

items.headline: India pulls the Diljit Dosanjh film 'Satluj' from streaming 48 hours after its release
items.summary: 'Satluj', based on rights activist Jaswant Singh Khalra who documented alleged extrajudicial killings in 1990s Punjab, was removed from ZEE5 two days after its July 3 debut. A government-appointed panel on July 11 upheld the ban citing sovereignty, and Sikh groups have staged gurdwara screenings in protest.

items.headline: India women crush England by 270 runs to win the first Test staged at Lord's
items.summary: India beat England by 270 runs on July 13 to win the first women's Test held at Lord's. Debutant Kranti Gaud took 5/37 to become the first woman on the Lord's honours board, and Yastika Bhatia's 113 was the first Test century by a woman at the ground; England were bowled out for 186.

items.headline: Counter-terror police lead the Ann Widdecombe murder inquiry, calling it a 'targeted attack'
items.summary: Former Conservative minister and Reform UK figure Ann Widdecombe, 78, was found dead with serious injuries at her Devon home. A 28-year-old British man arrested on July 11 was re-arrested on suspicion of terrorism as Counter Terrorism Policing took over, and on July 14 police called the killing a targeted attack.

items.headline: Twelve arrested over an alleged far-right plot targeting a 15,000-strong Muslim festival in Suffolk
items.summary: Counter-terrorism police arrested 12 people over an alleged far-right plot against the UK Ijtima gathering at Shrubland Hall in Barham, Suffolk, which drew about 15,000 people and was cut short on police advice. Eight men are held under the Terrorism Act; Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood said the response undoubtedly saved lives.

items.headline: Study estimates more than 2,700 excess deaths in England and Wales from the May-June heatwaves
items.summary: A rapid analysis by the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine, Imperial College London and the Met Office estimated over 2,700 heat-related excess deaths in England and Wales during the record May and June heatwaves, attributing roughly 42% to human-caused climate change.

items.headline: Investors trim UK gilt holdings, wary that Burnham could 'do a Truss'
items.summary: With Andy Burnham days from entering No 10, Rathbones said on July 14 it had sold long-dated gilts across a £9.8 billion multi-asset portfolio to guard against fiscal irresponsibility, while Jupiter, Neuberger Berman and Royal London are avoiding longer-dated UK bonds until the next chancellor's first budget.

items.headline: Sudan court sentences RSF chief Hemedti and 15 commanders to death in absentia
items.summary: An anti-terrorism court in army-held Port Sudan on July 13 sentenced RSF leader Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo (Hemedti) and 15 commanders to death in absentia for war crimes and crimes against humanity, centred on the 2023 killing of West Darfur governor Khamis Abbakar. It is the first conviction of the RSF's top leadership since the war began.

items.headline: Israel and Lebanon hold a sixth round of US-brokered talks in Rome on a troop pullout
items.summary: Israeli and Lebanese delegations opened two days of US-brokered talks in Rome on July 14 to implement a June framework deal, focusing on pilot zones near the Litani River where Israeli forces would withdraw, Hezbollah would disarm and Lebanese troops deploy. President Joseph Aoun demanded an immediate start to an Israeli withdrawal.

items.headline: Fire tears through a Bangkok beer hall near Chatuchak, killing 27
items.summary: A fast-moving fire engulfed the Rong Beer Na Lat Phrao beer hall in Bangkok's Chatuchak district late on July 12, killing at least 27 people and injuring 63, with 22 in serious condition. It was the Thai capital's deadliest blaze in 17 years, and investigators are examining the cause.

items.headline: Water-bombers battle a wildfire in France's Fontainebleau forest as Europe's heat persists
items.summary: More than 400 firefighters and water-bombing planes fought a wildfire that burned over 800 hectares of the Fontainebleau forest south of Paris on July 13, closing the A6 motorway. Spain's Almeria wildfire death toll rose to 13, and scientists estimated about 10,000 heat-related excess deaths across Europe over the past month.

items.headline: Nigeria rescues 39 schoolchildren and six teachers abducted 56 days earlier in Oyo
items.summary: Security forces freed at least 39 schoolchildren and six teachers 56 days after they were seized from three schools in Oyo state's Oriire district; eight kidnappers were arrested and no ransom was paid, the presidency said. One abducted teacher was killed in captivity, and President Bola Tinubu vowed to get justice.

items.headline: DeepSeek in talks to raise $1.5 billion at a $71 billion valuation ahead of a China IPO
items.summary: Chinese AI lab DeepSeek is in early talks to raise about $1.5 billion at a roughly $71 billion pre-money valuation and has begun preparing for a possible mainland China listing, a month after closing a $7 billion round at about a $50 billion valuation.

items.headline: AI video startup PixVerse raises a $439 million Series C at a $2 billion valuation
items.summary: Singapore-based video-generation startup PixVerse closed its Series C at a total of $439 million, with Alibaba and Mirae Asset joining an extension that pushed its valuation past $2 billion. The company reports more than 150 million registered users.

items.headline: BIS warns AI's debt-fuelled investment boom risks turning to bust
items.summary: The Bank for International Settlements said the AI build-out ranks among the largest tech-driven investment booms in US history, with the five biggest hyperscalers on track to spend more than $1 trillion across 2025-2026, and warned that circular financing and rising debt leave the sector exposed to a protracted bust.

items.headline: Anthropic and OpenAI press Washington to treat AI 'distillation' as a security threat
items.summary: Anthropic and OpenAI are urging US policymakers to treat adversarial model distillation as a national-security issue, with Anthropic alleging Alibaba generated 28.8 million outputs from its Claude models via roughly 25,000 fraudulent accounts. The House Foreign Affairs Committee has advanced the Deterring American AI Model Theft Act.

items.headline: Chinese open-weight models overtake US models in Hugging Face downloads
items.summary: TechCrunch reports Chinese open-weight models accounted for 41% of Hugging Face downloads this spring, surpassing US models, and that the six most-used models on OpenRouter are all Chinese open models from firms such as Tencent, DeepSeek and MiniMax.

items.headline: JPMorgan posts a record $21.2 billion quarterly profit on booming equities trading
items.summary: JPMorgan reported its highest-ever quarterly net income of $21.2 billion for Q2 2026, lifted by a $4.6 billion one-time gain on its Visa stake. Adjusted earnings of $6.14 a share beat the roughly $5.85 consensus, and equities-trading revenue jumped 86% from a year earlier to $6.03 billion.

items.headline: Goldman Sachs sets an all-time equities-trading record with a $7.4 billion haul
items.summary: Goldman Sachs reported Q2 2026 net revenue of $20.34 billion and diluted earnings of $20.98 a share, nearly double a year earlier, driven by a record $7.42 billion in equities trading, the third straight quarter its equities desk set an industry record. Shares rose about 9%.

items.headline: IBM suffers its worst-ever day, sliding about 25% after a Q2 earnings warning
items.summary: IBM shares plunged about 25%, their steepest drop on record, after preliminary Q2 results showed revenue of $17.2 billion and adjusted earnings of $2.93 a share, below the $17.85 billion and roughly $3.02 expected. CEO Arvind Krishna cited software and infrastructure weakness, dragging ServiceNow and Salesforce lower too.

items.headline: US consumer prices fall 0.4% in June, cooling annual inflation to 3.5%
items.summary: US consumer prices fell 0.4% in June, the biggest monthly drop since April 2020, pulling annual inflation to 3.5%, below the 3.8% expected, as gasoline prices fell about 10%. Core CPI was flat on the month at 2.6% year-on-year, and Treasury yields slid as traders trimmed September Fed-hike odds.

items.headline: Citigroup profit jumps 45% to $5.8 billion but shares fall on spending plans
items.summary: Citigroup posted Q2 2026 net income of $5.8 billion, or $3.15 a share against $2.73 expected, on revenue of $24.8 billion, its best quarterly revenue in a decade, with equities trading up 45%. Shares fell nearly 6% after management flagged higher second-half investment spending.

items.headline: India beat England by six wickets in the first ODI at Edgbaston
items.summary: India chased 259 to win by six wickets, reaching 262 for 4 in 45.2 overs at Edgbaston on July 14 to take a 1-0 series lead. Axar Patel was player of the match for his 4 for 62 and unbeaten 57, with Washington Sundar 52 not out; Joe Root's 76 not out had lifted England to 258.

items.headline: Maria Sakkari reaches the round of 16 at the inaugural Athens Open
items.summary: Playing one of the first WTA events held in Greece in decades, home favourite Maria Sakkari opened with a 6-0, 7-6 win over Polina Kudermetova on July 13, taking the first set in about 24 minutes. She next faces Britain's Harriet Dart.

items.headline: Top seed Andrey Rublev reaches the Bastad semi-finals
items.summary: Chasing his first title of the season, top seed Andrey Rublev beat Andrea Pellegrino 6-3, 6-2 in his opener at the Nordea Open in Bastad, then got past Jesper de Jong to reach the last four on the Swedish clay.

items.headline: Zheng Qinwen opens her Athens Open campaign with a straight-sets win
items.summary: Zheng Qinwen began her Athens Open run on July 13 with a 7-5, 6-1 first-round win over Jessica Bouzas Maneiro, part of a strong hard-court field at the new WTA event that also features Maria Sakkari and Alycia Parks.

items.headline: Update: Verstappen's camp opens 2027 talks with McLaren as F1 heads into Spa race week
items.summary: Sky Sports F1 reports Max Verstappen's camp has opened talks with McLaren over a 2027 switch as F1 heads into the Belgian GP weekend at Spa (race Sunday, July 19). Sitting seventh and 58 points behind George Russell, Verstappen looks likely to trigger his Red Bull exit clause by the August break; boss Laurent Mekies said Red Bull must convince him to stay.

items.headline: Webb's fourth-anniversary image reveals a galaxy scarred by an ancient collision
items.summary: To mark four years of science, NASA released a new James Webb Space Telescope image of Centaurus A, 11 million light-years away, whose warped dust lanes trace a major galaxy merger roughly 2 billion years ago. Webb's infrared view resolved individual stars around the active galactic core.

items.headline: Euclid telescope spots the two most ancient quasars yet seen
items.summary: ESA's Euclid space telescope has found 31 of the most ancient quasars known, including two record-holders whose light dates to when the universe was just 670 million years old, about 5% of its current age. The haul roughly doubles the number of quasars known from that early epoch.

items.headline: Semaglutide slowed markers of biological ageing in a controlled trial
items.summary: In a randomised, placebo-controlled trial of 108 adults published in Nature Communications, semaglutide, the drug in Ozempic and Wegovy, slowed several epigenetic ageing clocks, including a roughly 9% slower pace on one measure. Researchers call it the first randomised human evidence that a GLP-1 drug may influence ageing pathways.

items.headline: NASA's Perseverance rover clocks a full marathon of driving on Mars
items.summary: NASA's Perseverance rover passed 26.2 miles of total driving on Mars, reaching the marathon mark on its 1,890th Martian day while exploring terrain west of Jezero Crater. An orbiter image captured the rover and its tracks; it covered the distance in about five years and four months.

items.headline: NASA modelling cracks the mystery of the Sun's razor-thin tachocline
items.summary: NASA's COFFIES science team reported global simulations showing that the Sun's tachocline, the thin shear layer between its rigidly and differentially rotating zones, is kept thin by the dynamo's own fluctuating magnetic field. The layer underpins the 22-year solar cycle that drives space weather.

fun_fact.headline: Glass is not a slow-moving liquid
fun_fact.body: Contrary to a popular myth, glass is not a slow-moving liquid. The story that medieval cathedral windows are thicker at the bottom because the glass has oozed downward over the centuries is false; those panes were simply uneven when made. Ordinary glass is an amorphous solid, and genuine flow at room temperature would take far longer than the age of the universe.
fun_fact.source: Corning Museum of Glass / materials science consensus

puzzle.title: Six Sticks, Four Triangles
puzzle.body: You have six matchsticks, all exactly the same length. Arrange all six so that they form exactly four triangles, where every side of every triangle is one full matchstick (no bending, breaking, or overlapping).
puzzle.approach: Two triangles laid flat on the table only ever give you two; the breakthrough is to stop thinking in a single plane.
puzzle.answer: Build a tetrahedron (a triangular pyramid). Three sticks form the triangular base; the other three stand up from the corners to meet at a single apex above the centre. All four faces are equilateral triangles of three full sticks each - four triangles from six sticks.

word_puzzle.title: Hidden in the Mix
word_puzzle.body: Rearrange the letters of each phrase into a fitting word/phrase: 1) DIRTY ROOM (9); 2) CASH LOST IN ME (12); 3) HERE COME DOTS (12); 4) ELEVEN PLUS TWO (13).
word_puzzle.approach: Each clue is an anagram of its answer, and the phrase hints at the answer's meaning.
word_puzzle.answer: 1) DORMITORY; 2) SLOT MACHINES; 3) THE MORSE CODE; 4) TWELVE PLUS ONE (which, like ELEVEN PLUS TWO, also equals 13).
